problems.memo_sentence: The paper explicitly compares quantum QUBO-based feature selection against classical baselines such as Random Forest feature importance and mutual-information–based methods (including MI-Spearman), reporting that the quantum approaches consistently or at least slightly outperform these classical methods in terms of F1 and Gini.
problems.source_evidence:
Abstract: "Extensive experiments show that feature selection using QUBO on quantum computers consistently performs better than the other classical methods."

Discussions: "Our results have shown that FS using QUBO on a Quantum annealer consistently performs better than popular classical features selection methods. Also, for almost all the cases, training ML with quantum selected features performs better than training it with the full dataset."

Results – Small dataset: "With k = 25 selected features, classical MI-Spearman dominates for F1 score and Pearson QUBO dominates for gini." and "Among the classical methods, MI-Spearman performs well when large number of features are selected."
problems.explanation: The memo adds the qualifier "or at least slightly" and implies per-dataset, per-metric dominance, whereas the paper’s own summary claims unqualified consistent superiority of QUBO methods and in the detailed results actually notes a case where a classical MI-Spearman method dominates F1. The memo thus slightly overstates the robustness of QUBO’s advantage relative to the nuanced results.

problems.memo_sentence: Across multiple fraud and default datasets, the authors report that QUBO-based quantum feature selection generally performs as well as or better than classical feature selection methods when evaluated via F1 and Gini scores on downstream models.
problems.source_evidence:
Abstract: "Extensive experiments show that feature selection using QUBO on quantum computers consistently performs better than the other classical methods."

Discussions: "Our results have shown that FS using QUBO on a Quantum annealer consistently performs better than popular classical features selection methods. Also, for almost all the cases, training ML with quantum selected features performs better than training it with the full dataset."

Results – Small dataset: "With k = 25 selected features, classical MI-Spearman dominates for F1 score and Pearson QUBO dominates for gini." and "Among the classical methods, MI-Spearman performs well when large number of features are selected."
problems.explanation: The memo summarizes that QUBO methods perform at least as well as classical baselines across datasets, but the detailed results show at least one regime (small fraud dataset, F1 at k=25 and larger k) where a classical MI-Spearman method is best. This makes the memo’s blanket "as well as or better" characterization slightly stronger than what the results strictly support.
